receipts.first_text_witness: There's a couple in your neighborhood right now doing everything right. Hazel, 34, makes $82,000 in marketing. Nico, 36, makes $90,000 in IT. Combined, they're pulling $172,000 a year, which puts them in the top 25% of American households. And a smart mirror gym in the garage they used twice. And every month, when the bills clear, they look at each other with that specific quiet panic of people who genuinely don't understand how they're still this broke.
receipts.last_text_witness: to sleep, ask yourself one question. If one of these two paychecks disappeared tomorrow, what would actually happen? Would you adapt, or would the trap snap shut? Because the answer to that question is the only one that matters. If this was the financial reframe nobody else gave you. Do me a favor and let the next person find it, too. Subscribe and I'll see you in the next one.

primary_source_receipts.locator: Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi, The Two-Income Trap (Basic Books, 2003)
primary_source_receipts.finding: Compares a 1970s single-earner family with an early-2000s dual-earner family; the dual earners have about 75% more income but slightly less discretionary income after fixed costs and taxes.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Book not re-read; family figures by analyst recall; publisher URL approximate.

primary_source_receipts.locator: Fisher and Johnson, The Two-Income Trap: Are Two-Earner Households More Financially Vulnerable? CES-WP-19-19
primary_source_receipts.finding: Two-earner married couples in 1999 were more likely to file for bankruptcy in 2002-2004 than other married couples; they have a higher average propensity to consume.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Summary only; the 10% effect size was not confirmed; release month approximate.

primary_source_receipts.locator: Bank of America Institute paycheck-to-paycheck analysis (2025)
primary_source_receipts.finding: Nearly a quarter of households (about 24%) estimated to live paycheck to paycheck by account data.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Reused from NICK_241; lower-income 29% not confirmed; page date approximate.
